_comment: Scopes Pylance/pyright to FIRST-PARTY code. Two reasons, and the second matters more than the warning that
(1) Volume. The workspace holds ~250 first-party .py files and 13,116 under .venv, so the editor was
indexing site-packages as if it were project source. That is the 'large number of source files'
advisory: a performance complaint, not a correctness one.
(2) DUPLICATE MODULE TREES, which is the real hazard. This repo deliberately keeps several copies of the
archive/, and loose scripts under runs/. With those indexed, auto-import happily offers
'from models.ecoli.processes.polypeptide_elongation import ...' resolved against the ARCHIVED copy, and
the editor reports no error. In a repo whose whole subject is knowing which artefact a number came
from, an IDE silently binding a symbol to the wrong copy of a module is the same defect class in a new
venvPath/venv are set rather than just excluding .venv: excluding it would stop imports resolving at all.
This keeps it as the ENVIRONMENT while removing it from the indexed workspace.
NOT VERIFIED against pyright itself — no pyright binary is installed here (no PATH entry, no npx cache).
The shape follows the documented schema; confirm in the editor that imports still resolve and that
auto-import no longer offers model_overlay/ or vendor/ paths.
